title: The bench never starts a worker, so it measures nothing
what: In the bench scenarios the session delegates to a worker (as the delegate rule requires), so a change to the build tier changes what runs; add-function and small-script pass under the active setup.
why: Claude's usage advice (23 Oct) said give workers a cheaper model; the bench of workers on Haiku could not answer it: no scenario started a worker under either setup, so both setups did the same work and cost the same ($0.95 vs $0.93). Every model or effort change for build/fix tiers is unmeasurable until this is fixed.
failing_case: `relay bench active --set models.build=haiku --tag cheap --runs 1` (report ~/.relay/bench/2026-10-23T13-31-54Z/report.md): grader delegated-to-a-worker fails "started: none" in all 3 scenarios under both setups; add-function 0.40 and small-script 0.33 under both (function-exists, test-written, script-runs fail).
pass_cases: The same bench shows a worker started in add-function and small-script under both setups, both scenarios pass under the active setup, and the two setups' worker model differs in the report's model usage.
